page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4mds_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family designed for workloads that demand high per-core performance and large memory allocation. Running on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions.

Hardware resource allocation is heavily weighted toward memory capacity, delivering 336.0 GB of RAM, or 84.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed through a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD designed for low-latency temporary storage or caching. The instance does not include a GPU, and public IPv4 addresses are not bundled standard.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 2357.0 and high single-threaded compression rates. Conversely, aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the physical core count, as observed in a multi-core Geekbench score of 5278.0 and low multi-core decompression rates. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show modest throughput, recording 36.33 GB/sec for 256MB reads.

The instance provides qualitative cost advantages for software environments with pricing models tied strictly to core counts. By packing massive memory capacity and high clock speeds onto just 4 vCPUs, it avoids licensing overhead for large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include licensed relational databases, in-memory caching systems, electronic design automation (EDA), and data manipulation jobs.

A defining feature is its memory density, supplying 336.0 GB of RAM alongside a direct-attached 945 GB local NVMe SSD, with zero integrated GPUs.
